Assault - Retribution.name: Assault: Retribution
Assault - Retribution.summary: Assault: Retribution is a 3D platform shooting game that takes place across seven futuristic levels, includes two playable characters with alternate routes, analog control, and memory card support. You can't spell action, adrenaline or assault with out an "A," so go out and kick a few.

Battle Arena Nitoushinden.name: Battle Arena Nitoushinden
Battle Arena Nitoushinden.summary: The Toshinden cast goes back to school, as Toshinden Kids enters the arena...school arena that is. Select your favorite character in their youthful appearance and take on the rival fighters with all your might. 4 New characters appear for the first time in the series!

Gensou no Artemis.name: Gensou no Artemis: Actress School Mystery Adventure
Gensou no Artemis.summary: A first person perspective adventure game in which the player takes the role of a detective that has to investigate a murder in an actress school.

Momotarou Dentetsu V.name: Momotaro Dentetsu V
Momotarou Dentetsu V.summary: Momotaro Dentetsu V is a video game in the Momotaro Dentetsu series of board game-style video games, genre released in 1999 by Hudson Soft for PlayStation. The game was only released in Japan.

Neo Atlas.name: Neo Atlas
Neo Atlas.summary: Neo ATLAS is a reimagining of Artdink's home computer Atlas series, with 32-bit era upgrades to graphics and gameplay. Neo ATLAS is a reimagining of Artdink's home computer Atlas series, with 32-bit era upgrades to graphics and gameplay.

Slayers Wonderful.name: Slayers Wonderful
Slayers Wonderful.summary: Slayers Wonderful is a role-playing video game developed by TamTam and released by Banpresto for the PlayStation in 1998 exclusively in Japan. It features key voice actors from the Slayers anime versions and a story supervised by the Slayers author Hajime Kanzaka. The game was a big commercial success but received mixed critical reception.

World Stadium 2.name: World Stadium 2
World Stadium 2.summary: The second entry in the World Stadium series (after World Stadium EX), a PlayStation spin-off from Namco's Family Stadium series of baseball games. A handful of fictional teams compete alongside real Japanese league teams and players with cartoon graphics and simple gameplay.
